note: Edit this file to publish BCIEA announcements. Items below are general awareness content, not BCIEA events.

items.title: October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month
items.text: Every October communities worldwide promote early detection and access to care. Talk with family, neighbours and your community health worker.

items.title: Know what is normal for you
items.text: Breast awareness means knowing your own breasts and seeking advice when you notice a new or unusual change.

items.title: A change is not always cancer, but do not wait
items.text: A new lump, skin change, nipple change, unusual discharge or underarm lump should be assessed by a health professional.

items.title: From worry to care
items.text: Patient navigation helps you move from awareness to assessment, referral, treatment and follow-up with a human navigator beside you.

items.title: Your privacy, your choice
items.text: You can ask questions before consenting. Only authorised staff see case data, and you can ask to withdraw consent.

items.title: Severe bleeding, collapse or trouble breathing
items.text: Do not use the chat. Go to the nearest emergency service immediately.
